Agreed next steps to share reports and controls spreadsheet and schedule engineering follow-up for KMS integration.

transcript:
Date: 2026-10-21 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Emily Carter (CISO - Northwind), Marcus Lee (Head of IT), Sana Patel (Compliance Manager)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:04] Emily: Emily here.
[00:05] Marcus: Marcus on the line.
[00:06] Sana: Sana, hi.
[00:08] Jordan: Great. So the objective today is to run through Redwood's SOC 2 / ISO posture, make sure we can give you the artifacts you need for your attestation, and cover KMS and data residency questions. Priya is our security engineer, she'll jump into technical bits.
[00:20] Priya: Hi, thanks. I'll start with a high level: we maintain a SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO 27001 summary — customers get access to the Trust Center where they can download reports and open an evidence request for specific controls.
[00:32] Emily: When you say Trust Center, is that the portal with per-customer evidence? We need the raw evidence for a couple of controls for our auditors.
[00:38] Jordan: Yes, the Trust Center link is in the notes, I'll share after this call. It exposes the SOC 2 Type II PDF, and you can request access to the evidence portal. Typically we provide redacted artifacts and a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to SOC 2/ISO clauses.
[00:52] Marcus: Sounds good. How granular is the mapping? Our auditors want control IDs and sample artifact names.
[00:58] Priya: We provide a controls mapping CSV with control ID, description, evidence name, and a pointer to the artifact in the evidence portal. For some items we provide screenshots, for infra bits we provide config snippets or audit extracts. Occasionally names are redacted for multi-tenant items but we can often provide tenant-specific logs when you have a dedicated deployment.
[01:18] Emily: Ok, separate question: our encryption policy requires BYOK and HSM-backed keys for highly sensitive PHI. What's Redwood's posture?
[01:26] Priya: We support BYOK via KMS integrations. For hosted we integrate with cloud KMS providers; for Private or Dedicated we can enable customer-managed keys — there's an HSM option for on-prem or dedicated HSM providers. Transit is TLS 1.3, at-rest is AES-256. We'll share the KMS integration guide.
[01:44] Sana: Do you offer a bring-your-own-HSM flow? We have internal HSMs and strict key custody requirements.
[01:50] Priya: For on-prem Private deployments, yes, you can use your HSM and we can configure the runtime to call your key store. For hosted, we offer limited BYOK where keys are stored in a customer KMS project; full HSM wins are possible with Dedicated or Private arrangements and contractual terms.
[02:06] Marcus: What about audit logs — retention and integrity? Our compliance requires immutable logs for user activity and admin actions for 3 years.
[02:14] Priya: Default retention is 1 year in the hosted product, but we have add-ons for extended retention up to 7 years in the observability/archival tier. Logs are exported to an append-only store, with integrity checks. For Dedicated/Private you can export to your SIEM or S3 buckets under your control.
[02:31] Emily: And are logs tamper-evident? We need chain-of-custody for a subset of logs.
[02:36] Priya: We produce signed hashes of log bundles on export and store them with an index; for high-assurance setups we can implement an external attestation workflow — it's part of the enterprise compliance package.
[02:48] Marcus: Ok, RBAC and SSO — we use Okta and SCIM for provisioning. Are there role templates and SCIM?
[02:55] Jordan: Yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync. RBAC is fine-grained — you can create roles for Viewer, Operator, Admin, and also route-based permissions for models and datasets. We'll share the SSO/SCIM guide.
[03:09] Sana: For our auditors, we also need to see role change history and admin approvals. Is that captured?
[03:15] Priya: Yes, admin actions are audited and we capture who approved role changes, with timestamps. That lives in the audit log and can be exported.
[03:23] Emily: Data residency — our patient data must stay in us-east-2. Does Redwood host in specific regions or can you guarantee region-hosted data?
[03:31] Jordan: We have region controls — hosted customers can pick region endpoints; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment so you maintain the data plane in your VPC in us-east-2. For hosted we offer a best-effort region pinning and assurances in the contract.
[03:47] Marcus: Could you run benchmarks for latency if we pin us-east-2? We need numbers for SLAs.
[03:52] Priya: Yes, that's a follow-up engineering task — we'll scope a short perf test with representative prompts.
[03:58] Speaker 1: (mumbled) can you also clarify log retention pricing?
[04:02] Jordan: Sure, it's an add-on. We'll include the pricing sheet with retention options in the follow-up.
[04:08] Emily: On ISO 27001, do you maintain an ISO certificate or just a controls mapping?
[04:14] Priya: We maintain an ISO 27001 summary and undergo annual audits; the certificate and the scope statement are available to customers under NDA via the Trust Center. The controls mapping ties ISO clauses to our implemented controls and evidence.
[04:26] Sana: Great. For vendor risk questionnaires, can you produce templated answers?
[04:31] Jordan: Yes, we have standard VRQ response packs — SOC 2 + ISO attestation answers — and a security questionnaire pack that covers encryption, access control, and incident response. We'll attach that.
[04:40] Marcus: Incident response — do you provide notification SLAs and playbooks?
[04:43] Priya: We have an incident response policy, notify customers per contractual SLA (e.g. 24-72 hours depending on severity), and provide a post-incident report and timeline. Playbooks are summarized in the security docs.
[04:56] Emily: A couple of nitty-gritty asks from auditors: 1) mapping of control IDs to our internal control names; 2) sample proof of key rotation; 3) list of third-party subprocessors and their SOC coverage. Can you provide those?
[05:09] Priya: Yes — we'll include the subprocessors list, key rotation samples, and the mapping. Some detailed artifacts require us to redact other tenants, but we'll give tenant-specific extracts where possible.
[05:24] Jordan: Quick recap of asks: Emily — you want SOC 2 Type II and access to the evidence portal; Sana — BYOK/HSM details and role-change history exports; Marcus — log retention options and perf benchmarks for us-east-2. We'll send a controls mapping CSV and evidence pointers.
[05:38] Emily: That matches our list.
[05:40] Jordan: Great. Next steps in the notes — Jordan will share links and Priya will drop the mapping spreadsheet. We'll aim to reconvene after your team reviews, and then schedule the KMS integration deep dive.
[05:53] Marcus: Thanks, everyone.
[05:55] Sana: Thanks.
[05:56] Jordan: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes / Links: Trust Center: https://redwood.ai/trust-center | KMS guide (internal): https://redwood.ai/docs/kms-integration | Controls mapping template: attached via CRM

End of transcript.
